record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: QSOs defined by factorized heredity coefficients
record.original_question: Consider QSOs whose heredity coefficients factor as P_{ij,k} = a_{ik} b_{jk} for matrices A = (a_{ik}) and B = (b_{jk}) satisfying the stochasticity and symmetry constraints required of P. Equivalently, the operator has coordinates (V(x))_k = (sum_i a_{ik} x_i)(sum_j b_{jk} x_j). Develop a structural and dynamical theory for this class of QSOs, including how it generalizes Volterra QSOs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E=\{1,2,\dots,m\}$ and let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m_{\ge 0}:\sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(V(x))_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j,\qquad k\in E,$$
where the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy
$$P_{ij,k}\ge 0,\quad P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k},\quad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j,k\in E.$$

Consider the subclass of QSOs whose heredity coefficients admit the factorization
$$P_{ij,k}=a_{ik}\,b_{jk}\qquad\text{for all }i,j,k\in E,$$
for some real matrices $A=(a_{ik})$ and $B=(b_{jk})$ satisfying the constraints that make the resulting $P_{ij,k}$ a valid (nonnegative, symmetric in $(i,j)$, and stochastic in $k$) heredity tensor. Equivalently, $V$ has coordinate form
$$(V(x))_k=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ik}x_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{j=1}^m b_{jk}x_j\Big).$$

Develop a structural and dynamical theory for this class of QSOs. In particular:
(i) characterize all pairs of matrices $(A,B)$ for which the above factorization defines a valid QSO;
(ii) describe the fixed points, $\omega$-limit sets, and long-term dynamical behavior of the iterates $V^n(x)$;
(iii) determine in what precise sense this class generalizes the class of Volterra QSOs (those satisfying $P_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$), and identify the new dynamical phenomena that arise outside the Volterra case.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific publications were located that develop a structural/dynamical theory for the factorized class P_{ij,k}=a_{ik}b_{jk}. Related work treats Volterra QSOs, F-QSOs, permuted, and dissipative QSOs, but the targeted factorization problem appears unaddressed in the literature retrieved. Status: open.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of QSO classes (Volterra, F-QSO, etc.) and dynamics; no treatment of the a_{ik}b_{jk} factorization is highlighted.
status_evidence.claim: The factorized class is not among standard developed subclasses.

status_evidence.title: F-quadratic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a different structured subclass (F-QSO) of QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Related structured subclasses are studied but not the a_{ik}b_{jk} factorization.
